description: A graduate study of how production game engines are structured for speed and scale: entity-component-system design, cache-aware data layout, job systems, custom allocators, asset pipelines and profiling. Students build and benchmark the core of a small engine in the code runner and visualise cache and memory behaviour.
outcomes: Design an entity-component-system and justify its storage layout against an object-oriented alternative with measurements.
Predict and measure the effect of data layout on cache misses and frame time.
Implement a job system with dependencies and reason about data races, ordering and determinism.
Write custom allocators and a streaming policy that meet a stated memory budget.
Build an asset pipeline with incremental builds and hot reloading of data and scripts.
Profile an engine build on target hardware, set a frame budget and fix the largest bottleneck.

units.title: Engine architecture and entity-component-system design
topics: Engine subsystems and the main loop: fixed versus variable timestep and the accumulator pattern
Entity-component-system: entities as ids, components as data, systems as functions
Component storage: archetypes versus sparse sets, queries and iteration
Command buffers, deferred structural changes and event queues between systems
Comparing deep inheritance, composition and ECS on a worked game feature

units.title: Data-oriented design and cache behaviour
topics: The memory hierarchy: cache lines, associativity, misses and the cost of a cache miss
Array-of-structures versus structure-of-arrays and hot/cold data splitting
Alignment, padding, false sharing and prefetching
SIMD basics and batching work for vectorisation
Cache-friendly spatial structures: uniform grids, flat BVH and sorting by locality

units.title: Job systems and multithreading
topics: Thread pools, tasks and dependency graphs of jobs
Work-stealing deques and load balancing
Atomics, memory ordering and lock-free queues
Data races, deadlock and designing for determinism
Frame pipelining: simulation, render and audio threads; parallel-for patterns

units.title: Memory allocators and streaming
topics: Linear, stack and pool allocators and per-frame arenas
Free-list and buddy allocators; fragmentation and compaction
Handles, generation counters and safe references instead of raw pointers
Asset streaming: level-of-detail paging, prefetch and memory budgets
Memory profiling and budgets for low-end Android phones and browser targets

units.title: Asset pipelines and hot reloading
topics: Importing, cooking and packing assets; platform-specific formats
Asset databases, stable identifiers, dependency graphs and incremental builds
Compression, texture formats and bundle layout for download size
Hot reloading of data, shaders and code
Serialisation, reflection and versioned save formats

units.title: Scripting and tools integration
topics: Embedding a scripting language: binding native functions and ownership across the boundary
Script cost, coroutines and when to move logic out of scripts
Editor tooling: inspectors, property reflection and undo systems
Data-driven design: configuration files, tuning tables and live editing
Debug tooling: developer console, in-game profiler overlay and deterministic replay

units.title: Cross-platform builds and profiling
topics: Build systems and toolchains; abstraction layers for platform differences
Platform abstraction of graphics, input, audio and file systems
Frame budgets, CPU and GPU profiling, flame graphs and sampling versus instrumentation
Performance regression tests and benchmarking in continuous integration
Optimising for mobile and WebAssembly targets: thermal limits, battery and download size

units.title: Deterministic simulation and engine integration
topics: Deterministic simulation: fixed-point maths, seeded randomness and replay
Physics and collision pipeline integration: broad phase, narrow phase and solver ordering
Rendering architecture: scene graph versus render graph and visibility culling
Published engine post-mortems: lessons from architecture decisions that aged badly
Capstone: assemble and benchmark a mini engine core against a stated frame budget

schedule.title: The game loop and ECS foundations
schedule.exercise: Implement a fixed-timestep loop with an accumulator, then sketch the data structures for entities, components and systems and give the cost of a query that visits two component types.

tasks.title: Code a fixed-timestep game loop with an accumulator and print the number of updates per rendered frame at 30, 60 and 144 fps
Implement a minimal ECS with entity ids, two component arrays and a movement system, and run it on 10,000 entities
Implement sparse-set component storage with dense iteration and compare insertion, removal and iteration time against a hash map version

schedule.title: Deferred changes and design comparison
schedule.exercise: Model a poisoned-and-burning status effect for monsters three ways (inheritance, composition and ECS) and compare how hard each is to extend with a new effect.

tasks.title: Add a command buffer to your ECS so entities destroyed during iteration are removed safely after the system finishes
Build an event queue between a collision system and a damage system and verify event order over 1,000 simulated frames
Implement the same 20,000-entity feature as inheritance and ECS, benchmark both over 1,000 frames and report time per frame and lines changed to add a feature

schedule.title: Caches, layout and vectorisation
schedule.exercise: Predict the number of cache misses when summing one field across 1,000 structs of 64 bytes versus a packed array, then measure the time difference.

tasks.title: Step through a direct-mapped cache with a stride-1 and a stride-16 array walk and count hits and misses for each
Convert a particle update from array-of-structures to structure-of-arrays and measure speed-up for 1 million particles over 100 frames
Demonstrate false sharing with two threads updating adjacent counters, fix it with padding and report the time before and after

schedule.title: Job systems and concurrency
schedule.exercise: Draw the dependency graph of jobs for a frame (input, AI, physics, animation, render submission) and compute its critical path on four cores.

tasks.title: Build a thread pool that runs 100 tasks and prints how many each worker thread completed
Add work stealing to the pool and compare finish time on a workload of tasks with very uneven durations against a shared queue
Find and fix a data race in a given multi-threaded particle system, then prove the fix makes 100 runs produce identical results

schedule.title: Allocators and safe references
schedule.exercise: Compare malloc with a pool allocator for 100,000 same-sized objects and explain why a generation counter prevents use of a stale handle.

tasks.title: Implement a linear per-frame arena allocator, reset it every frame and verify allocations never overlap across 1,000 frames
Implement a pool allocator for fixed-size entities and benchmark 1 million allocate and free pairs against the language default
Implement handles with generation counters and show that access to a destroyed entity is detected rather than reading reused memory

schedule.title: Fragmentation, streaming and budgets
schedule.exercise: Design a streaming plan for a 12 km open world on a phone with 1.5 GB usable memory, with the number of chunks resident, the load radius and an eviction rule.

tasks.title: Watch a free-list allocator serve a sequence of 20 allocations and frees and note where external fragmentation first blocks a request
Simulate chunk streaming along a player path with a load radius and least-recently-used eviction, and report hit rate and peak memory
Tune texture and mesh budgets for a low-end phone so peak memory stays under 1 GB while the visible quality score drops by under 10 percent

schedule.title: Importing, cooking and the asset database
schedule.exercise: Draw the dependency graph of a model, its material and two textures, then explain which files are rebuilt when one texture changes.

tasks.title: Write a tool that converts a text mesh file into a packed binary format and verify a round trip returns identical vertices
Build an asset database with stable ids and hash-based change detection so that only modified assets are rebuilt on the second run
Pack 200 small assets into one bundle with an index, compare load time and download size against separate files and justify the layout for slow networks

schedule.title: Hot reloading and serialisation
schedule.exercise: Specify a versioned save format for a farming game that must still load saves from version 1 after fields are added in versions 2 and 3.

tasks.title: Serialise a game state of entities to JSON and back, then diff the loaded state against the original
Watch a data file and reload tuning values into a running loop within one frame without restarting the process
Write migration functions that load version 1, 2 and 3 save files into the current format and test with 12 sample saves including corrupted ones

schedule.title: Scripting, tools and debug facilities
schedule.exercise: Decide which of ten gameplay behaviours should be native code, script or data, and justify each choice by frequency, cost and designer need.

tasks.title: Move enemy health, speed and damage into a table loaded at start-up and change three values without recompiling
Embed a small interpreter, expose three native functions to it, and run a script that spawns and moves entities
Record player input per frame, replay it into a deterministic simulation and verify that the final state matches the original run exactly

schedule.title: Build systems and platform layers
schedule.exercise: Design the platform abstraction interface for file access, input and windowing so the same game code runs on Linux, Windows and a browser build.

tasks.title: Write a build script with targets for debug and release configurations and show that only changed files are recompiled on the second run
Define an abstract file-system interface with two implementations, one real and one in-memory, and run the same tests against both
Draw the layered architecture of an engine with a platform layer and mark which modules may depend on which, rejecting three illegal dependencies

schedule.title: Profiling and performance engineering
schedule.exercise: Set a 16.6 ms frame budget across systems, profile a supplied frame trace, and propose the single change that frees the most time.

tasks.title: Instrument five systems with scoped timers, print a table of milliseconds per system over 600 frames and flag any over budget
Write a benchmark harness that runs the physics step 100 times, reports mean and 99th percentile and fails when it regresses by over 10 percent
Analyse a trace of frame times from a mid-range phone, find thermal throttling in the plot and recommend quality settings that hold 30 fps

schedule.title: Determinism, physics and rendering architecture
schedule.exercise: Compare a scene graph with a render graph for a deferred renderer, and list what must be fixed in a simulation for two machines to agree frame by frame.

tasks.title: Replace a floating-point movement update by fixed-point arithmetic and a seeded random generator, and show identical results across two runs
Implement a uniform-grid broad phase and narrow-phase circle test for 5,000 bodies and count pair tests against brute force
Implement frustum culling over a flat bounding-volume array and measure objects drawn and time per frame for 50,000 objects

schedule.title: Capstone: mini engine core
schedule.exercise: Present your mini engine: architecture diagram, benchmark table against the frame budget, and one decision you would reverse after the post-mortem readings.

tasks.title: Run the capstone benchmark scene of 10,000 entities and record frame time, memory and entity count in a results table
Draw the architecture of a published engine post-mortem as a diagram, marking the decision that caused the later problem
Integrate ECS, job system, arena allocator and profiler into one build, reach a 16.6 ms frame at 50,000 entities and document each optimisation
